newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares maintain week-long record run.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares maintain week-long record run.

text.p: Egyptian share prices maintained their week-long foray into record territory on Monday in turnover swollen by the state's sale of shares in a leading paints and chemical firm.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index firmed 0.83 percent to 362.61 points as an increasing number of foreign investors mined the market for prospects.
Volume was 215.92 million pounds ($63.5 million), dominated by the state's sale of 1.44 million shares worth 167.37 million pounds in Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN.

The state had initially offered 1.3125 million shares or 13.125 percent of the firm but apparently decided to increase the stake sold after the offer was more than three times oversubscribed. The firm's shares closed unchanged at 139.76.
Star performer Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was the day's top gainer, rising 21.49 pounds to close at 451.49 in heavy trading worth 4.8 million pounds.
Cement firms continued to feature strongly in the day's trading as did a few pharmaceutical firms.

Amriyah Cement was the sector's best performer for the second day, rising 1.4 pounds to 83.3 in trading worth 6.3 million pounds. Helwan Portland Cement also rose 0.14 pounds to 77.89 on turnover of 2.8 million pounds.
Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries was heavily traded with shares worth 4.7 million pounds changing hands but shares ended unchanged at 200 pounds.
Alexandria Pharmaceutical and Chemical Industries rose 3 pounds to 80 in brisk trade.
The popular milling shares were also active with Central and West Delta Flour Mills rising 5 pounds to 105 and Upper Egypt Flour Mills closing 1.35 higher at 86.6.

Related firm General Silos and Storage rose 3.68 pounds to 77.18 after the company said it had increased pre-tax profits for the first half of 1996/7 to 38 million pounds from 26 million in the same period last year.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 594.75 points from 589.64 points on Sunday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 241.67 from 239.76.
Out of the 89 shares traded, 50 gained, 16 lost and 19 ended the day unchanged.
